clue.text: One awfully roguish chap who worked on Malvern Hills

definitions.text: chap who worked on Malvern Hills

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of the following word are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rascally fellow once laboured on the hills above Malvern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles ROGUISH, placed after I. The Malvern Hills here are not a workplace but the title of a story in Kazuo Ishiguro's collection Nocturnes.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist wrote a short story titled Malvern Hills, so he is the man who worked on it.

clue.text: Prompt quote given by Irish nationalist leaders

indicators.note: leaders means taking the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A rousing slogan is offered by the heads of an Irish independence movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' is a verb, to urge someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone to act is to stir them up or urge them on.

clue.text: What criminals like Parker do first in the East on occasion

annotationWithheld.why: What criminals like Parker do first in the East on occasion (6): HEISTS fits every crossing and 'What criminals like Parker do' defines it, but no parse of 'first in the East on occasion' gives its letters
annotationWithheld.clue: What criminals like Parker do first in the East on occasion

clue.text: Disgusting hotel stayed in by Cambridge university writer

indicators.note: the university pieces come before the hotel letter, the guests arriving at their lodging

parts.note: gross means disgusting
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Cambridge academic author puts up at a revolting hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge university' suggests England; it is MIT across the Atlantic. George Grossmith co-wrote The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: George Grossmith co-wrote the comic classic The Diary of a Nobody with his brother.

clue.text: Parvenu in Du Maurier novel having a sudden change in direction

parts.note: Rebecca is Daphne du Maurier's best-known novel
a sharp turn is an abrupt change of direction

explanation.surface: An upstart character in a du Maurier book swerves suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the social climber of Thackeray's Vanity Fair, Becky in full; du Maurier only supplies her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's Becky climbs from poverty into high society, the classic social upstart.

clue.text: Article about high-class, deep philosophical work

indicators.note: about tells us the article word is turned round to face the other way

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
U is the old label for upper-class usage
the deep is a poetic name for the sea

explanation.surface: A grammatical article sits around an elevated, profound treatise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AN into NA. The definition is Sartre's first novel, La Nausée, a key existentialist text.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartre's novel of that title is a founding text of existentialist philosophy.

clue.text: Vessel impounded in Barcelona or Tarragona

indicators.note: impounded in says the vessel is locked up within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A ship has been seized in one of two Catalan ports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the body's main artery, a blood vessel leaving the heart.

clue.text: Strange-looking Shetland scribe who wrote a biography of Napoleon

definitions.text: scribe who wrote a biography of Napoleon

indicators.note: strange-looking says the island name's letters take on an odd new appearance

explanation.surface: An odd-looking writer from the Northern Isles produced a life of the emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Stendhal, who served in Napoleon's army, wrote a Life of Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist served under Napoleon and wrote an unfinished Life of him.

clue.text: Beastly type breaking into worker's home to get food?

definitions.text: Beastly type breaking into worker's home to get food?

parts.words: Beastly type breaking into worker's home to get food?
parts.note: reads like a burglar raiding a labourer's house, but the beast raids a nest of worker insects for a meal

explanation.definitionFit: This mammal tears open termite and ant nests to lick up the insects it lives on.

clue.text: Energy low? Doctor must visit this Malawian writer

parts.note: chi is the life energy of Chinese thought

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside the place visited, so the doctor's letters go within the word for low

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Someone feeling drained needs a doctor to call on this African author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy low?' reads as feeling tired, but 'low' is a cow's sound. Steve Chimombo is a Malawian poet and novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Chimombo was a poet, novelist and dramatist from Malawi.

clue.text: One such as Dorriforth has his nose stuck in Time

parts.note: someone who pokes their nose into things pries

explanation.surface: A bookish character keeps his nose buried in a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like the magazine; it is just T. Dorriforth is the Catholic cleric hero of Elizabeth Inchbald's novel A Simple Story.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorriforth in Inchbald's A Simple Story is a Roman Catholic cleric, an example of the calling.

clue.text: Murdoch publication one dropped in basket by French chopper?

definitions.meaning: a novel by Iris Murdoch, not a Rupert Murdoch newspaper

definitions.text: one dropped in basket by French chopper?
definitions.meaning: the guillotine's victims' heads fell into a basket

explanation.surface: A tabloid owned by a press baron is chucked away by a French helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch publication' suggests Rupert's newspapers; it is Iris Murdoch's 1961 novel. The 'French chopper' is the guillotine.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris Murdoch wrote a novel of that name, and a guillotined victim's cut-off top fell in a basket.

clue.text: General from America chasing after little singer

indicators.note: a chaser comes behind, so the American letters follow the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
US is short for United States

explanation.surface: A general from the States pursues a small songster.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus was a Roman general before he became emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus commanded the Roman legions that besieged Jerusalem before becoming emperor.

clue.text: Conservative dope with artist's an unbelievable prophet

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
and means together with
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A Tory fool teams up with a painter who turns out to be an incredible seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbelievable' is the joke: Cassandra's curse was that her true prophecies were never believed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan seer was cursed so that nobody would ever believe her accurate predictions.

clue.text: "This is one of the —s of wine, it makes a man mistake words for thoughts" (Samuel Johnson)

definitions.text: "This is one of the —s of wine, it makes a man mistake words for thoughts" (Samuel Johnson)

parts.words: "This is one of the —s of wine, it makes a man mistake words for thoughts" (Samuel Johnson)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Boswell's Life of Johnson; the gap wants a word for a drawback or downside

explanation.definitionFit: Johnson called wine's habit of passing off talk as thought one of its drawbacks.

clue.text: "Probably since the end of the — Age, there have been three kinds of people in the world, the High, the Middle, and the Low" (Orwell)

definitions.text: "Probably since the end of the — Age, there have been three kinds of people in the world, the High, the Middle, and the Low" (Orwell)

parts.words: "Probably since the end of the — Age, there have been three kinds of people in the world, the High, the Middle, and the Low" (Orwell)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation from Goldstein's book in Nineteen Eighty-Four; the gap wants the late Stone Age

explanation.definitionFit: Orwell dates the class system back to the close of the New Stone Age, the period of early farming.

clue.text: Aristocrat with good books about unknown Egyptian tourist

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman

indicators.note: about puts the good books around the unknown

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A nobleman with improving reading matter considers a mysterious visitor to Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibsen's hero wanders through Morocco and Egypt in Act IV of the play, visiting the Sphinx.
explanation.definitionFit: In Act IV of Ibsen's play the hero travels as a sightseer to Egypt and the Sphinx.

clue.text: Time family member gets German work about the Great War

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
a son is a family member

explanation.surface: A relative serving time receives a German book about the First World War.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRD is British prison slang, from 'birdlime' rhyming with 'time'. Sebastian Faulks's 1993 novel is set in the trenches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebastian Faulks's novel follows a soldier through the trenches of the First World War.

clue.text: Old New York author with no hatred? That makes a change!

indicators.note: the exclamation tells us the letters are switched around into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A writer of old Manhattan who bears no grudge is a refreshing novelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That makes a change!' rearranges WITH NO HATRED. Old New York is the title of Edith Wharton's 1924 set of novellas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharton wrote the novella collection Old New York and chronicled that city's society.

clue.text: One in the thrall of differently-dressed Viola?

definitions.text: One in the thrall of differently-dressed Viola?

indicators.note: in puts the numeral for one inside the rearranged name
differently-dressed says the name appears in new clothes, its letters rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Who falls under the spell of Viola disguised in men's clothes?
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night, Viola dresses as the page Cesario, and the countess falls for her. The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's countess falls hopelessly for Viola while Viola is disguised as a young man.

clue.text: Bell, perhaps of yellow metal, Zulu traded for piece of Tupperware

indicators.note: traded for swaps one letter out and another in

parts.note: bronze is a yellowish alloy of copper and tin
Z is Zulu in the phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: piece of means only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A bell made of yellowish alloy is swapped for a plastic food box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like the thing that rings; the Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The three Brontë sisters published under the pen names Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell.

clue.text: Left-wing broadcast about husband like Weasley?

parts.note: red means socialist or left-wing
aired means broadcast

explanation.surface: A socialist programme about a married man resembles a Hogwarts pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places H inside AIRED. The Weasleys of Harry Potter are famous for their ginger hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ron Weasley and his family all have ginger hair in the Harry Potter books.

clue.text: What one will have to be for a late do?

definitions.text: What one will have to be for a late do?

parts.words: What one will have to be for a late do?
parts.note: a late-night party keeps you from sleep, but a do for the late, the dead, is a funeral gathering

explanation.definitionFit: A party running late needs guests not asleep, and a wake is the gathering for the dead.

clue.text: Bartleby's one left in fish restaurant at front

indicators.note: in puts the letter for left inside the fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: at front means only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Melville's scrivener orders fish at a restaurant counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside IDE, giving IDLE. Melville's Bartleby the Scrivener 'would prefer not to' do any work.
explanation.definitionFit: Melville's Bartleby refuses all work, the very model of a layabout.

clue.text: Old master with outer-desire for alchemist's assistant

indicators.note: outer says the desire word goes round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: a yen is a longing
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: An old painter with a strong craving works for a gold-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old master' looks like a painter; it is O and MA, wrapped by YEN. In Chaucer's Canon's Yeoman's Tale, the Canon is an alchemist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Canon's servant in The Canterbury Tales is his alchemical helper.

clue.text: Young wealthy type last to join Buchanan's football team

parts.note: young means new
the haves are the well-off

indicators.note: last to means only the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A rich youngster is the latest recruit to a footballer's side.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Buchanan of The Great Gatsby played football at Yale, whose home is the Connecticut city named here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Buchanan was a Yale footballer, and Yale's teams play in the Connecticut city.

clue.text: Swedish linesman flipping hit on foremost of Norwegian backs

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for hit over so it reads the other way

parts.note: to get someone is to hit them

indicators.note: foremost of means only the opening letter is taken
backs turns the word for on round

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A Swedish line judge flips, striking a Norwegian defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns GET into TEG; 'backs' turns RE into ER. A linesman here is a writer of lines: Esaias Tegnér was a Swedish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Esaias Tegnér was a celebrated Swedish poet, a writer of verse lines.

clue.text: A lawyer going to Irish county to see Carstone's wife

parts.note: DA is a district attorney
Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

explanation.surface: A lawyer travels to the west of Ireland to visit a client's widow.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's Bleak House, Richard Carstone secretly marries his cousin Ada.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bleak House, Richard Carstone secretly weds his cousin and fellow ward Ada.
